      • Time:

      • Flanders in Points streams DHMV II — the Flemish government’s national LiDAR survey, flown 2013–2015 at ≥ 8 points/m² — straight into this browser tab. No install, no download, no desktop GIS.

        The whole cloud is one COPC file on a plain web server: no tile pyramid, no database, no backend. The browser requests the couple of megabytes of that file your current view needs, and nothing else.

        A research demonstration built at Ghent University on public open data. Every point here is DHMV II, re-encoded — the survey is not ours.

        • How it works
      • 1 DHMV II
        100k+ open LAZ tiles, ~3.3 TB, fetched onto HPC storage.
        2 copc_converter
        An out-of-core Rust merge into a single COPC octree — 21.5 hours, 372 core-hours.
        3 This viewer
        Potree-Next, reduced to what one deployment needs, reading HTTP byte ranges.
        • Built on
      • Digitaal Vlaanderen The DHMV II survey itself — flown, processed, and released openly.
        Hobu, Inc. The COPC specification. One file, no tiling, no special server.
        360-geo / copc-converter The converter that merged the whole tile collection into one octree. MIT.
        Markus Schütz Potree and Potree-Next — a decade of rendering massive point clouds in a browser, and the COPC support underneath this page. AGPL-3.0.
        Ghent University HPC Compute, storage, and patience for a 21.5-hour job.

        Base map © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); geocoding by Photon/Komoot. Bundled browser libraries keep their own licences.

        • Licence

      • The code is AGPL-3.0-only, inherited from Potree-Next. Because you are using it over a network, § 13 applies and the source of this deployment is public: github.com/flol3622/DHMVII_potree-next.

        The data is not ours to license. DHMV II is Flemish government open data, and its core condition is attribution to the data owner. Check the source before redistributing anything derived from it.

        Use it, fly through it, screenshot it, cite it. Suggested attribution:

        Point cloud: DHMV II, © Digitaal Vlaanderen, open data. Viewer: Flanders in Points, AGPL-3.0, derived from Potree-Next (Markus Schütz). Format: COPC (Hobu, Inc.). Conversion: copc-converter (360-geo).

        • Funding

      • This work has been (partially) funded by the Flanders AI Research program, and carried out at Ghent University, whose HPC infrastructure provided the compute and storage the conversion needed.
